<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par116 />{{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁכַּ֫חַת}}, with Qimḥi, as the 3rd sing. fem. of the perfect; on the form, cf. {{GHGpar|44|f}}); or in relative clauses, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=5|translate=what I am doing}}, i.e. am in the act of doing; in a deliberative question, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=30}}; but especially often when the subject is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} (especially also if the subject be attached as a suffix to {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} as {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִנְּךָ}}, &c.), if it is intended to announce the event as imminent, or at least near at hand (and sure to happen), when it is called ''futurum instans'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=13|hidebook=1}} f., 48:21, 50:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=8|hidebook=1}}; with a participle passive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=21}}: cf. also {{GHGpar|112|t}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|q}}
Rem. 1. As the above examples show, a noun-clause with a participle as predicate may have for its subject either a substantive or a personal pronoun; in both cases the participle, especially if there be a certain emphasis upon it, may precede the subject. Also in noun-clauses introduced by {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} the subject may be either a substantive, or (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=7}}) a separate personal pronoun, or a suffix attached to {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}. In the same way, the subject may also be introduced by {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}} (''est'', see the Lexicon) with a suffix, and in negative sentences by {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} (''non est'') with a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־יֶשְׁךָ מוֹשִׁיעַ|translate=if thou wilt save}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אֵֽינְךָ מְשַׁלֵּחַ|translate=if thou wilt not send}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=11}}.—In such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹ הַנְּטוּיָה|translate=the stretched out hand is his}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּטוּיָה}} is not, like {{GHGheb|text=נְטוּיָה}} in 9:11, 16, &c., the predicate (in which case the participle could not take the article), but the subject; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=6}} (cf. {{GHGpar|126|k}}), where the participle with the article likewise refers to the present, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=16}}, where it refers to the past. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=8}} and 21:11 even in relative clauses after {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|r}}
2. To give express emphasis to an action continuing in the ''past'', the perfect {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}} in the corresponding person is sometimes added to the participle, and similarly the imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִֽהְיֶה}} (or the jussive {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}}, or the imperfect consecutive) is used to emphasize an action continuing in the ''future'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּקָר הָיוּ חֹֽרְשׁוֹת|translate=the oxen}} (cows) ''were plowing''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=6}}; the same occurs with a passive participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִֽהְיֶה}} with a participle is found e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=2}}; the jussive in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=12}};<ref>A jussive is practically to be supplied also in the formulae of blessing and cursing, {{GHGheb|text=בָּרוּךְ|translate=blessed be ...}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=26}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אָרוּר|translate=cursed art thou}} ... 3:14, &c.</ref> and {{GHGheb|text=ויהי}} with a participle in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=1|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|s}}
3. The ''personal pronoun'' which would be expected as the subject of a participial clause is frequently omitted, or at least (as elsewhere in noun-clauses, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=32}}) the pronoun of the 3rd pers. {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=8}} (the participle always after {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}); cf., moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=17}}, 19 ff., 25:2, 26:7.—{{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} is omitted in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=3}}; in a relative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=2}}.—The personal pronoun of the 2nd pers. masc. ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}) is omitted in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=10}}; the 2nd fem. ({{GHGheb|text=אַתְּ}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=16}} (where, however, for the participle {{GHGheb|text=וְנׄכַ֫חַת}} the 2nd fem. perf. {{GHGheb|text=וְוֹכַ֫חַתְּ}} is to be read); the pronoun of the 1st sing. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=5}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=16}}; the 2nd plur. ({{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=24}} (if the text be right), 6:3, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=7}} (?). But these passages are all more or less doubtful.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|t}}
Of a different kind are the cases in which some undefined subject is to be supplied with the participle; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵלַי קֹרֵא|translate=there is one calling unto me}} (= one calleth; {{GHGpar|144|d}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=4|hidebook=1}}.—So with participles in the plur., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֹֽמְרִים}} sc. the taskmasters); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=23}} (in 33:5 the text is corrupt), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=7}} (?), 36:13, 37:11 (equivalent to ''sunt qui dicant'').<section end=par116 /><noinclude>
